utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm sorry about the delay because we have to share the courtroom with other cases. So there are some rumours floating on the floor, but anyway, let's begin. Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, and thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Krsnik: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you had a good rest. Can we pick up with where we left off tomorrow [as interpreted]? I'd like to have back on the ELMO that drawing. Yes. Can we go back to it? Do you remember the one?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Usher, will you please help me? [In English] Put it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, please will you take the pointer. My first question to you, Witness, is: Starting from the -- from this flyover over to the centre of Mostar, how far is that, approximately? I mean the west side, of course.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't be able to tell you that. I really do not know, sir. I don't know even approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how far are the first houses from west side of Mostar? Approximately. It doesn't really matter. Approximately.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the first houses in Rastani?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From this flyover where you started drawing this line, and then looking to the left, how far are the first buildings from Mostar, from the west part?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, houses stretch from Bakina Luka onward.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you could say that Rastani is a part of Mostar, couldn't we?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now, if we moved from this flyover to the hydro powerplant, approximately, of course, just roughly, how many kilometres would that be, that section of the front that you manned in Rastani up to the hydro powerplant, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: We held the line on the hill above the last houses, so I cannot really say how many kilometres. Because the front line did not follow either the railway tracks or the road, so that I cannot say exactly. I know where the front line passed, but ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And following, then, this red line, that is where you fortified -- I mean, you made some fortification, fortified positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, as far as I know, we were in the last houses, and perhaps a bunker here and there. Because I was not there. I wasn't on that front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now tell me: From which directions did the HVO advance on the 23rd, I mean its infantry? Were they advancing along the whole front line or ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, sir, from the curve up on the Raska Gora towards Dumpor's houses, so they were coming down from there. I don't know about any other directions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now tell me: Why did the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina attack Rastani on the 24th of August, wasn't it, the first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, sir, the BH army did not attack on the 24th of August. Well, excuse me. Yes. I may have mixed up the dates, because you used the term "liberated" Rastani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is: Why did you in fact attack Rastani, or rather, who did you liberate it from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, that is clear. That is what HVO says. When they take an area, they say they have liberated it. So the same term was used in the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But who did you liberate Rastani from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the HVO, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And had you managed to keep Rastani, would you then be at the back of the defence of the west side of Mostar? Would that mean --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do not know what were the plans of the BH army. I wasn't really in the know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You said that the BH army and the HVO were together in Bijelo Polje right up to the 30th of June. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which means, sir, that the unity was preserved there, and for a month those men were together. Now, my question is: Why -- whom did you attack and who did you liberate Bijelo Polje from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I told this Honourable Court yesterday that there was a shortage of food in the town by that time already, and for that reason, the BH army tried to link up with Sarajevo so as to have some communication and so that food supplies could get in. That is as far as I know, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I fully understand what you are saying, but that is not what I asked you. In Bijelo Polje, there were no problems whatsoever because the HVO and the BH army were together, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, we who were in the old part of the town or, rather, in East Mostar, we could not get through. And I'm telling you that we were really very short of food. Food was really running out, and that is why the BH army ordered to provide this linkup.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness VV, why link up if you are all together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm repeating, sir, that we had no food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I understand. You're repeating this for the third time. But I'm asking you about Bijelo Polje, Witness VV, where the forces were together.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: But, sir, we could not get through to Bijelo Polje from East Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know that one night members of the BH army turned their -- targeted their former allies and massacred 25 members of the HVO and imprisoned others in the camp at Bijelo Polje? Are you aware of that on that particular day, the 30th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware, sir, that there were any massacred people. I do not know about that. I repeat it. I know there were captured members of the HVO. About any massacres, I do not know. And, sir, I do not know who turned their barrels on whom, because on the 9th of May, sir, the HVO was the first one to start shooting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to know where our learned colleague is leading to us. What is the relevance of some HVO members being arrested or executed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Krsnik. Would you please answer this question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, and I shall be gratified to do so. In his examination-in-chief, the Prosecutor asked a number of questions, and Bijelo Polje was even circled, and that is why I think that this witness should be subjected to verification during the cross-examination. Secondly, when answering the questions of the Prosecution, the witness said that the BH army attacked and liberated Bijelo Polje. So my question was only, "And what happened then?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, as a rule before this Court, we only want to hear those things which are directly related to the subject matter of this case. I hope you could focus your cross-examination on the part which is related to your client. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me -- and was then the road opened, the way opened to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, over Ravna Gora, over the mountain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Sir, the road, yes, was free, but the HVO was on the other side and in the vicinity so that we went across the mountain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the HVO beyond, behind the hydro powerplant too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the right bank of the Neretva, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Witness VV, why did you attack Kalik on the 9th of May, that is, the west part of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. What place?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. I may have misnamed the place. That part in West Mostar. What did you say? Kalik, Kalionik -- Oh, no, no, no, no. Zalik. Sorry. Sorry. Apologies. My fault. Zalik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, I really did not answer that question, because I was just a plain soldier, and all I did was execute the orders of my command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you that because I was surprised to hear how many things you know being a plain soldier. So my question to you is: How is it you know about the front agreements and withdrawals on the positioning of front lines, being a foot soldier? How do you know all that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, believe me, but almost everybody knew that in Mostar. I think it was also on Radio Mostar, counsel, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, then I'm asking you why didn't you relocate your command to your front lines? Why did you leave it in the centre of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I wouldn't know, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many men participated with the BH army in this attack on Zalik and other parts of Mostar in the night between the 9th and 10th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know how many men did the BH army have deployed around flats in the west side of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why did the BH army attack the northern camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, sir, it was that same operation when Bijelo Polje was taken. And I suppose the reason was the same. I'm not really -- I don't know very much about it. It is my guess that that was so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those captured during this operation, were they put up in the elementary school in Mostar? I mean captured HVO soldiers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know, they were put there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the only camp? Were there other camps on the east side of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the east side of Mostar, sir, I am not aware of any camp except --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean except the 4th Elementary School?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, except for 4th Elementary School.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there also Croat civilians in that camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know, sir, because I never once visited that school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness VV, I do not want to keep you long today, but last night and this morning when I tried to recapitulate it all, I tried to make concise my cross-examination. But I'd like to go back to Siroki Brijeg, if you don't mind. I do have a few questions about it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'll answer to the best of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Exhibit 26.8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness VV, my first question is: Do you recognise this area? Do you know what it is, where it is, and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I do not know this cell, sir, because in the civilian prison when we were taken there, it was dark and there were no lights. All I can remember is that there were some sponge mattresses on the floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't ask you where it is. I'm asking you if you can recognise it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recognise this cell because I was in those two places, at Siroki, but I spent in complete darkness here during 24 hours so that I could not see anything and therefore I cannot recognise anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And tell me, this company, this firm, this factory that they took you to, do you remember what the building looked like? Was it large, small, medium size? If you remember, of course.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, I cannot remember the building, but Siroki Brijeg is a small place. So I'd say that it was slightly larger than the buildings around it. Because we arrived by night, so that --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Tell us, were there any stairs taking you to the cellar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the room that you were in in the cellar, those rooms, there were walls between you and your colleague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said it already. It was metal. That is, it was a tin plate. So between me and my colleague was a tin plate, not a proper wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. And again you had a sponge mattress on the floor, or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we had were army cots, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this photograph here, this area here, it could be that you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the one that I'm looking at now?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot really say yes or no with any certainty. I cannot say that positively. But I do not see any cots here. But I mean, the size of the room, it could be it. And again, I do not see this tin plate which partitioned this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's only because of this cot and this tin sheet, but this tin could have been painted over in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: But, sir, I spent 24 hours in the darkness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: It seems to me that the witness has already answered this question. He did not see anything in the darkness. What did you see? These questions again. The witness recognises this cell. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. The response has already been given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think that's a reasonable response from the Prosecutor. You may skip this question, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, can I ask you a question? Where is that cell located? Which building is that cell?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This cell, Your Honour, is in the tobacco station. It is the old photograph. We saw it a number of times. And my question to the witness was whether we could recognise him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... that you are showing him a cell in the tobacco station, so the witness knows that. This cell that you're being shown is from the tobacco station. Just so that we're not tricking him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I must object. This is a photo of the cell of the MUP station. It is not fair to our witness to mislead him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, please, just a second. I do not want to have the repetition of the situation the other day, that I fear that we misunderstand each other and that some conjectures are made in advance, and that was not my intention. My question was fair and honest: Could he recognise this area? The witness answered as he did. My next question was whether he spent all his time in this cell. May I assume simply if the witness was in the cell? If the witness does not recall it, then nothing more than that. And the witness answered as he did answer, and that was a correct answer too. And this photograph, I think that the Honourable Court has seen this photograph at least ten times so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... seen this photograph before, and I wanted to get it clear: Is this a photograph of a cell in the MUP station, or is it a cell from the tobacco station?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a cell from the MUP station, from the police station at Siroki Brijeg. I asked him if he was there, if he could remember this cell, and he answered no. Because if you remember, other prisoners who we heard, some ten of them recognised the cell immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Yes, but this prisoner said he was held in darkness, he doesn't know what the cell looked like, and there was a tin partition between them and he slept in a cot. None of those features are present here. But I just wanted to make sure that when you show a photograph to him, that he knows where that photograph is from. So even though he doesn't recognise it, we can now let him know that it represents a cell in the MUP station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Witness VV: At the time when you talked with Mr. Naletilic, when you had your coffee and tea, do you remember what the person who brought this coffee and tea looked like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I know, sir, is that it was a young woman. She brought this tea and coffee and left the room immediately, so that I cannot describe her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me, do you remember any details from that room: a cabinet, a desk, a chair, how Mr. Naletilic was dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I remember that there was a desk there, that I sat on one side of the desk and he sat on the other side. What he was on, I don't know. I had been beaten, and my eyes were already shut from all the beatings. I could barely sit, let alone make keen observations about objects in the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. You cannot recall, for instance, even the hair colour of this young woman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall, she was dark-haired, but I don't recall. I think she had dark hair, but that would be about all, as far as the woman is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said that a soldier had brought you there to the room where Tuta was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he also in the room, or did he leave it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: He left, sir. He just brought me in and then left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me, please: When you were transferred to Ljubuski, the day that you came out in front of the building, that is, where you were being held, do you recall any details: the surroundings, the buildings? Was it a brick facade? Was it a painted facade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we came out of that building that morning, they moved us to another building, and then we were waiting in a hallway until the vehicles arrived, and then 15 soldiers came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. Let me interrupt you here. We know that. I wanted to ask you: You went from one building to the next. Were you looking around? Did you notice anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I was not on vacation in Siroki Brijeg. I was exhausted. I was barely walking. And in my statements to the Tribunal, I said that we were not even given water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that, and I do sympathise with you, and this is not a formal statement. I really sympathise with you on that. But still, you know, a person does not know where he is. So did you look around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that would have been the case under normal circumstances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. So you wouldn't be able to either recognise nor describe the other building either?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, except that I know that it was close by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in fact you do not know where you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was very clear, sir, that I was in Siroki Brijeg, but where exactly -- because given the circumstances in which I was, it is hard to describe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what we know with certainty is that you were in Siroki Brijeg; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how do you know that you were in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I said yesterday in my statement to the Trial Chamber that Kolobara said that we had to be brought alive to Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is the only basis on which you know that you were in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also recognised the central prison of Herceg-Bosna, sir, and I showed that to you yesterday. And as far as I recall, sir, in my evidence yesterday, I said that we had crossed a bridge and turned right. And I had been in Siroki Brijeg only once before that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, with your permission: It is solely on the basis of what Kolobara said; that, in fact, is the only reason why you're saying that you were in Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I recognised the building where I spent the night, the central prison. But if you were to take me to Siroki Brijeg now, I would be able to recognise it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, from that building where you spent the first night, you were taken in a car, in a van, to another location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. From that building, they took us to the civilian prison, and from the civilian prison, the next morning, brought us back to that building. We did not go anywhere else in these however many days we were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now, this car or this vehicle that you were in, was that a windowless vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, we were lying on the floor and we had about ten soldiers around us who beat us and provoked us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you see the bridge, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, these soldiers were saying, "There we are. We are crossing the bridge now. We're coming to the building now." This is how we knew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right, Witness. So listening to them, you came to these conclusions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would be all, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, this is going to be my last question. We can note -- we can freely say that you saw -- you did not see anything on that road with your own eyes or in Siroki Brijeg, but you heard about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I said we were lying on the floor in the van, both of us, and we were mistreated and beaten. And I recognised the civilian prison of Herceg-Bosna, which to me clearly meant that we were in Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to show you the picture 26.4 one more time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you see the picture? Tell me now, did they also mistreat you in front of this building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is so characteristic about this building that it stayed in your mind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing, sir, but inside the building quite a few things stayed in my mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Inside the building. Now that you recall the building, where did you sleep in the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a cell, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you enter -- I don't know exactly where it is. I know that we entered through this door, and I was taken into a cell, and the person who was with me was taken somewhere to the right. It was dark and there was foam mattresses on the floor, and that's where we were sleeping.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you don't know where those cells are inside the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the two police vehicles in front of the building, were there also such police vehicles in front of the building that you can see in this picture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall, and it was late at night, sir. And as I said previously, we were in such a shape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. And had you not seen these police vehicles on this picture, you would still have the same mental picture of that entrance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any cross-examination, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence of Vinko Martinovic has no good reason to cross-examine this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. I have no questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any questions from the Judges? Judge Clark. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Witness VV, I have a few questions to ask you that I would like some clarification on. Yesterday when you gave evidence, when you and your colleague were looking for the unit to whom to give them their supplies of ammunition, you said that you saw a group of civilians and some soldiers who appeared to be fanned out and the civilians were in front of them. Did you ever find out who the civilians were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Man in jeans and T-shirt whom I saw at that time I saw later on on the west side after I was exchanged on the 19th of March, and I did not know the rest of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Did you know what their role was there that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, Your Honours, no. But later when I was exchanged, this young man approached me and asked me whether I was taken prisoner at that time. I told him yes, and then he told me that he was a human shield at that time. In other words, he remembered my face at that time. And at that time, I did not remember his face; I only remembered the jeans and the T-shirt on him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Did you ever find out that one of these men that was there that day was able to contact the Red Cross and tell them of your whereabouts? Did you ever find that out, or do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I heard that when I was transferred to the prison in Ljubuski when the Red Cross arrived on the 26th of November, 1993. The lady of the Red Cross, when I gave her my name, she said, "Oh, we finally found you."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Did she appear to know of your whereabouts when you spoke to her? She knew about you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, from what I understood from what she said, she did not know where I was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: But she knew of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, as far as I know, she -- all I know is that she arrived on the 26th of November with another member and asked whether we had been registered by the Red Cross, and I said that we had not been. And she asked us for our names, and both my colleague and I gave her our names. And when she checked the names, she told us, "Oh, we finally found you."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Very good. Returning to Rastani, as you were coming up the hill and going towards Dumpor's houses were there any buildings or houses that were actually burning or smoking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, from Dumpor's houses up towards Pinjuh's houses, you could see smoke, a heavy, thick smoke. And where we were and the place we were taken prisoner, those houses around there had already been burnt down. So they were not burning at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: You see, Witness, the reason I'm asking you these questions is that we've heard evidence that a number of the houses in the area were the residences of Serbs which had been damaged or destroyed in an earlier part of the conflict. I was just -- I wanted to know from you, could you distinguish between those houses which had been burnt the previous year and other houses in the area? In other words, were they houses that had been burnt in the last 24, 36 hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Serbian homes had been burned during 1992, and these -- the houses that were on fire, you could see the smoke. They had not burnt down yet. They had been torched maybe an hour, couple of hours before. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you. And I don't know if you can answer this question. And of course if you don't know, I want you to indicate that to me. Do you know if the houses which were burning and which you describe as recently torched belong to any particular ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that, Your Honour. I did -- I did not know Rastani well, and I did not know who owned which house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you for your honesty. Now if I can bring you to Siroki Brijeg. You described to the Court and in cross-examination recently how you were taken to an office by a soldier. Were you told by that soldier where you were being taken or why you were being taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, the gentleman who came to get me in the basement just said, "Get up. You're coming with me," and took me up the staircase to the office where Mr. Naletilic was sitting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Now, when you described the place as an office, I appreciate that you were not in good shape. I appreciate that you weren't in a position to make acute observations. But can you go this far - and if you can't, it doesn't matter - can you go this far: Can you describe this room as an interrogation room or an office, an office, being where somebody has accumulated books and personal effects?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, as far as I could see under the circumstances, this was an office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Did the person who was sitting behind the desk and who ordered tea and coffee introduce himself to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, as far as I remember, he did introduce himself to me, Mr. Naletilic did, as commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Did he tell you his name, Mladen Naletilic, or did he say, "I'm commander Tuta"? Can you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I cannot say that, but I believe he said "Commander Tuta."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And when he ordered tea and coffee or ordered the girl to bring tea and coffee, can we infer from that that he actually offered you refreshment and gave you a choice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And when he was questioning you, was it -- you mentioned some of the things he asked, but was it in the nature of a military interrogation, that you were a soldier and he wanted information about army movements from you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, the gentleman only asked me about our commanders, their whereabouts, whether they were in Eastern Mostar or somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the next question I want to ask you about is the unpleasant incident where you were -- you were tortured. Do you have any idea whether your torturers were simply behaving cruelly and sadistically or whether they were seeking information from you? Were they asking you questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, they were asking questions of me. In other words, they would switch on the electricity for a couple of minutes, and then they would switch it up, and then they would ask me questions, and then after that they would again start all over, and they were laughing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Were the questions related to military activity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, these questions were - how shall I put it? - without any purpose. There were some military ones. There were some personal insults. They also were demanding that I should pray in their manner, and then they would laugh at that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I don't want to cause you pain. I understand what you're saying. You described on another occasion when an HVO officer with whom you had had contact when you were in the army and you were both fighting a common cause, you described how he came to speak to you, and he in particular sought information in relation to two HVO soldiers who had been engaged in a form of sabotage. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: How was his questioning to you as one military man to the other? How did he conduct that investigation or interrogation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, that soldier spoke with me in a very regular way, as if we were in some coffee bar or restaurant in town, in other words, without trying to provoke me or to insult me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Witness VV, thank you very much for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Clark. Any questions out of the Judge's questions? Yes, Mr. Krsnik. Further cross-examination by Mr. Krsnik:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you heard the question of Her Honour Judge Clark about the man who was wearing jeans and a T-shirt, you know, of the prisoner at Dumpor's houses. Do you remember what Judge Clark asked you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just in case, Your Honours, can we move to the private station for this question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, the place where you were taken prisoner, those Dumpor's houses, how many are they? Five, six, seven? If you can, sir. What is referred to as Dumpor's houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I think there's about 14 houses in Rastani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I'm only referring to the Dumpor's houses.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, these are all Dumpor's houses. There may be 13 or 14 families there. They're all called Dumpor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the houses where you were first in the cellar and then you were taken prisoner there, did anybody torch those?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said that before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. And now, just a final question: The person who asked you about these divers, was that Maka Radic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Maka Radic, when he was questioning you about this, did he come to visit you in that cellar, in that basement where you were in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The answer is yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, for giving your evidence. We all wish you good luck in your future. When the usher pulls down the blinds, he will show you out of the room.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage, are there any documents to tender? Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would like to tender the following documents, exhibits: P11.18, as marked as the witness; P26.4; P34.2, as marked by the witness; P34.10; P538.1; and P745.1. As for the documents P614, 677, P704, they have been already tendered before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, no, we don't have objections to maps, and down to 538.1. We have no objections to all the above. All the others - 745.1, 614, 677, and 704 - we object to these documents, and we shall submit it in writing within seven days. We have already made our objections earlier, but we shall continue with our standard practice; that is, within seven days I shall reason these objections. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Those documents which are not objected to are admitted into the evidence. Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence should also like to tender D1/42. This is the map as marked by the witness, when the witness drew this line through Rastani, and that was on Prosecutor's Exhibit 34.2. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I guess there are no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It is admitted into the evidence. It seems that we could have our early break. We'll resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It might just be most efficient. The next witness has asked for voice distortion, and perhaps we could at least get that started before, and then we won't have to break again. So if we could just ask for that to be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. That could be fixed during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours. Judge Clark, Judge Diarra. The next witness has requested protective measures in the nature of facial image distortion, voice distortion, and a pseudonym for security reasons. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I guess there are no objections from Defence counsel at this time. Thank you very much for your cooperation. Your request is granted, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, good afternoon. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. Good afternoon. Yes, I can. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Will you make the solemn declaration, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Scott. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I might inform the Chamber, while the adjustments are being made, that the evidence of this witness is particularly relevant to the following parts of the indictment: Background, paragraphs 10 and 11; superior authority, paragraph 17; general allegations, paragraphs 20 and 21; count 1, paragraphs 26, 27, 32, and 34; counts 9 through 12, paragraphs 45 and 49; count 18, paragraph 54; and count 21, paragraph 57. Examined by Mr. Scott:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you have heard the Chamber perhaps say that the protective measures that you've requested have in fact been granted. That means that your name will not be used in these proceedings in order to protect your identity, your face will not be shown, and your voice will be altered in such a way that hopefully it will not be recognised by anyone who might hear your testimony. So I will caution you for those reasons not to use your name or perhaps any -- the names of close family members when you testify, because if you do so, of course, that will tend to identify you. So with that in mind, the usher's now going to show you a piece of paper that in fact has your name on it, I believe, and without saying your name, can you just confirm for the Judges so then they know you are this person, that that is your name? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll try to ask the questions that might require private session for the most part right at the beginning, and so if I might please ask that we go to private session for a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we're going to go very quickly to the core part of your testimony, if you will, but I have two questions or so that I wanted to ask you before that. During your time in Mostar, during 1992 and 1993, were you familiar with a man named Milivoj Gagro?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes, I was. [redacted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Gagro at that time have a position in the Mostar city government?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes. He was the elected head of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Gagro himself was a person of Croat ethnicity; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time in 1992 when Mr. Gagro was replaced as mayor by a man name Jadranko Topic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: I think it was in -- yes, quite right. 1992. Mr. Jadranko removed Mr. Gagro and took his post. Both were members of the HDZ, but I guess they did not see eye to eye, because Mr. Gagro is quite a moderate person and I think they did not like him. I do not know the true reason why he was dismissed, but I know that he was and that Mr. Jadranko Topic became the head of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber, please, was that replacement, what you've just described, was that as a result of free elections, or how was it that Mr. Gagro was replaced by Mr. Topic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: I have already said that Mr. Gagro was the elected -- he was elected in the elections, because the HDZ, SDA, and SDS had won the elections. They distributed offices amongst them, and Mr. Gagro was elected the head of the municipality. And another, the second in rank, was -- I don't know who it was, but it was a Muslim. And then why they dismissed him, those in the HDZ, I wouldn't know exactly, but Jadranko Topic took his place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask my question this way: Did the Bosniak population of Mostar have any say? Did they have a chance to vote or select Mr. Topic as Mr. Gagro's replacement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: No. No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've already said that you don't -- you can't speculate as to all the reasons, perhaps, that Mr. Topic replaced Mr. Gagro, so I'm not asking you that. But can you tell the Chamber: Did you observe any differences in the policies, in the conduct of the government in the city of Mostar after Mr. Topic took over, in comparison to when Mr. Gagro was mayor?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, all these questions put to the witness call for speculation, because this witness was not in any body, political or party or electoral, so that any question asked of her in this vein calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe the first one, the previous one, is sort of speculation, but not the previous one -- this one. The question is that: "Did you observe any differences in policies in the conduct of the government in the city of Mostar after Mr. Topic took over, in comparison to when Mr. Gagro was mayor?" That's the personal experience from this witness, so this question is allowed. But before that question, that one is sort of speculation. But anyway, the witness has answered this question. I'll let it go. You may proceed, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you still recall the question, would you -- can you go ahead, please, and answer the question: If you saw differences in the Mostar government after Mr. Topic took control as mayor.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: To be quite frank, the situation was rather strange. I wouldn't be able to explain it properly, but it was somehow strange. It was odd. I mean, things that were happening in the town were quite odd.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I don't want to spend a great deal of time on this, but I think I must ask you: When you say there were things that were strange or odd, can you assist us a bit more than that? What was strange or odd, and why would you call it strange or odd?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. The relations between people changed completely. People around town started saying ugly things, and the whole situation in the town. Mr. Topic, I think, was a harder line in the HDZ. Well, I'm just an ordinary citizen, but I presume that Mr. Topic was carrying out all the decisions and orders of the HDZ. So that HDZ wanted to take over complete control over the town, and I think so that the whole situation was very difficult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, this confirms that the question invited speculation, because this answer is pure speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it's a fair response by this question. I don't want to go into private session, but she is a person in a position to be able to make her observations and what was happening in this location at this time. These are not technical, political speculations; they are observations of persons in that community. I think that's perfectly responsive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We also believe that. You may proceed, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, around this time, the same time, Witness WW - and just one or two more questions before getting to the 9th of May, 1993 - were you also familiar with -- and I'm not suggesting you knew this person in a personal way, but did you know of a man named Hadziosmanovic, who was also a political figure or leader in Mostar at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes. I think that gentleman represented the SDA, and he was more prone to defend the HDZ than the Muslim interests in the town, so that he allowed the signing of a document in which he turned over the town to the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a member of this community, did most of the Bosniaks consider that this Mr. Hadziosmanovic represent their views, or was it the view that he was out of step with the majority view?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honours. I really do not want to tax your patience. I do not know how is it possible to answer these questions except by speculation, because in view of the circle in which this lady was moving, I mean, she cannot speak on behalf of the broad Muslim community. If this does not invite speculation, then I really do not know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, the question is that as a member of this community. I believe that everybody who lives in that community will have an opinion concerning the leadership of that time. Let us hear what is the response from this witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, my question to you was: In your community and among the Bosniak people that you were familiar with, was there a view that Mr. Hadziosmanovic spoke for the majority of the Bosniak community, or what was your observation in that regard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: No, did he not. Mr. Hadziosmanovic did not protect the interests of the Bosniaks, of the majority of Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, moving to April 1993, just a few additional background questions. Do you recall, Witness WW, that the HVO, around the 15th of April, 1993, attacked the -- an ABiH unit that was then located at Hotel Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes. At the Hotel Mostar a clash took place between the BH army and the HVO because, I guess, the HVO wanted to take that part, because afterwards, when the separation line was established, because the Mostar Hotel is right on the separation line between the Croat and the Bosniak part of the town. And the conflict occurred not between the civilians but between the troops. And after that, certain meetings were held and some order was made to separate them, that is, that one should go to one side and others to the other side. And the army did as ordered, but the HVO, by night, entered the hotel and went into that hotel and stayed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm just picking up from the speed of the translation that you might be speaking just a bit fast. If you could possibly speak a bit more slowly so that the translation can be accomplished.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Am I fast? Yes, possibly. Possibly I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If you could think about speaking a bit more slowly, I'm sure it would assist. Thank you very much. Now, were you in your home in Mostar on the 9th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you briefly just tell the Chamber, in your own words, what happened that morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: On the 9th of May, 1993, around 5.00 in the morning, the shelling of the town started, and when all my family woke up - because we had already been through one war crisis, and we thought that it was over - we were caught by surprise as to what was happening now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear any broadcast on the television or radio that morning that you can tell the Chamber about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: No. I got up, switched on the radio. There was only Radio Mostar. That was the only communication medium in the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber at that point in time, by May of 1993, what group or faction controlled the radio station in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: The HDZ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during that morning of May of -- excuse me, the 9th of May, did you hear any broadcast about the attack on Mostar Radio?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes. Mrs. Zlata Brbor, a journalist and presenter, announced that the HVO was taking over -- was undertaking, was launching an armed attack against the BH army, that it would be over soon, that the population should not worry. But shortly after her, the radio station -- I heard over the radio Mr. Topic's voice, and he repeated that same thing, and also asked the citizens who were Muslims to put out white rags or cloth or flags or something like that and that then nothing would happen to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It may or may not be obvious, Witness, but what did you understand the significance of putting out the white flags or rags, or did Mr. Topic say anything more about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Well, I suppose that we should surrender.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to look out from your apartment that morning and see anything that was happening outside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: There was a lot of gunfire outside, and it was all targeting the left bank in the town of Mostar. And shortly after these news -- after this news programme, columns and columns of people started passing by, some half dressed, some simply if their underwear, and they were heading towards the left bank, towards the old city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness WW, I want to tell you that if reliving these things causes you any suffering, I apologise for that. Of course, it's necessary and helpful for the Judges to hear your testimony, but I regret if it causes you any pain. If you do come to a moment when you would like to take a break or collect yourself, I'm sure the President would allow some moment to do that. Moving ahead that morning, did anyone come to your apartment, and can you tell us what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Well, sometime after 6.00 or 7.00, around that time, somebody knocked on our door. My husband -- my husband opened the door, and in front of the door there were up to seven men, armed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the seven men that were then standing outside of your flat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: When the first soldier asked my husband what was his name, my husband told him his name, and he answered, "Balija," and ordered us to come out. And that was Mr. Ernest Takac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, we're going to go forward with your story in a moment, but let me ask you: Among the soldiers that were outside or came to your flat at that moment, apart from Mr. Takac, did you recognise any of the others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Because I'm -- because I was the first - that is, my flat is the first flat in that building - I then saw Mr. Martinovic, Mr. - I've already said so - Ernest Takac and a short gentleman whom they called Dolma.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said just now -- when you said one of them was Mr. Martinovic, do you recall a first name and any nickname associated with that man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Later, after I was kicked out of the apartment and all that, when I was en route to the Heliodrom, when I was on the bus, I learned that his full name was Vinko Martinovic and that his nickname was Stela. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the one named -- or nicknamed Dolma, did you know at the time or have you learned any other name associated with that man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Later on I learned that Mr. Dolma was named Pehar, P-e-h-a-r, last name, and I don't know his first name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've given some explanation already, but I want to ask you again: How is it that you recognised that day Ernest Takac; Martinovic, Stela; and this man Dolma?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Because they were already well known in the city. People were saying all kinds of things about them. I had never met them before until that day. And Mr. Vinko Martinovic, Stela, was the chief man in the HOS, so that more or less everybody in town knew him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A clarification on that, please. When you say he was the chief man in something called HOS, do you mean at that time, or that he had been in that position sometime previously?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: I don't know. Believe me, the HOS did exist in the period of war when the JNA was there and attacked Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's continue on with: After these men came to the door and asked your name, what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: When Mr. Takac heard what my husband's name was, he took the plaque off the door with his rifle and he ordered us all to come out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're saying now -- when you say "the plaque off the door," was this a plaque that had your family name on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell the Chamber, please: How was it that Mr. Takac removed that from the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: With a rifle. With a rifle butt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many apartments were in your building, or flats, if you recall, please, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: In my building? In the building where I lived, there were 16 apartments. Right, there were 16 apartments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell the Judges, please: Of those 16 flats, approximately how many were occupied by Bosniak families?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I omitted to ask this earlier. My apology.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I don't think it's sufficiently identifiable that it warrants private session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you and your family are persons of Muslim origin or ethnicity; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: The same thing that happened to me. We were all kicked out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you see -- or can you tell the Chamber whether anything happened that morning to the Croat families in the same building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My apologies, Witness. It's a problem with my question and not your answer. When I said, "can you tell," let me rephrase it. Was anything done or happening to the Croat families in the building that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened next? Where did they take you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: When I came out in front of the building with my family, I saw other people who were in front of our building standing there, and they were all Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see again, as you gathered in front of the building, the group of you, any of these same men who you told us about a few minutes ago: Mr. Takac, Dolma, or Mr. Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Mr. Takac was standing there, also Mr. Martinovic was, while other soldiers were collecting people from other buildings and bringing them over to my building, because that is where our building was, out on the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, based on what you saw, based on your observation, could you tell if these HVO soldiers -- did any of them act as if or was treated by the others as if he was in charge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stela. Mr. Martinovic was in charge. And all the soldiers, as they were collecting people, after they were done with that, they were all going over to him and saying that everything was all right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber, please, what you saw happened to him that morning about this time?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Witness. Mr. President, it may be out of an abundance of caution. If I could ask that that name be redacted. I wasn't really sure if it was necessary, but probably it's safer if it is redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, you have to be very cautious about certain questions which might reveal the identity of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I didn't think it would tend to identify so much this witness, but out of concern, potential concern for that other person. And again, out of abundance of caution, I think it's best that it be redacted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apology, and certainly my fault, not the witness's fault.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This man -- and I don't want you to use the name again, because, as you've just heard, we're not going to mention his name at this point. But what did you see then happen to him next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: A black Mercedes was parked in front of the building. And Mr. Stela asked him whose Mercedes it was, and the gentleman answered that it was his.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Mr. Stela asked for the keys to the car, and because this gentleman didn't have them, he said that somehow he could start the car by connecting wires.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: One of his soldiers entered the car and started it and then drove the car away someplace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell the Chamber, before we move on with the events on the 9th of May, can you tell the Judges, please, did you see this same black Mercedes at a later time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes. After I came back from the Heliodrom, I started working again. And coming back from work, across from the coffee bar that belonged to Mr. Stela, I saw a black Mercedes on fire, and I recognised it by the licence plates. [redacted]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apology for the microphone. If we can redact the name. I'm sorry, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, perhaps you can assist us. You've made reference to seeing this same black Mercedes in front of Stela's coffee bar, as you describe it. In connection with your being released from the Heliodrom, can you give the Chamber some idea in terms of -- with reference to the 9th of May, approximately how much later was it? How much time passed before you saw this Mercedes in front of Stela's coffee bar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: I came out of the Heliodrom on the 15th or 16th of May, and I started working right around the beginning of June. It wasn't long after the 1st of June. I don't know the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. That's fine, Witness. Thank you. After you were taken outside and after the Mercedes was driven away, the group of you were collected and some of you were taken off in the direction of the Velez stadium; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes, the whole group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell us a bit more about how that was done. Did you all go as a group, and did there come a point in time when the women and children were separated from the men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: When they led us out in front of the building --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. The last two or three questions are very leading and very suggestive. I would just like the Prosecutor to rephrase his questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we don't believe that it is a leading question, because this is the natural course of the event that happened along this line. Yes. You may proceed, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I was trying to be a bit more efficient, but I'm happy to proceed otherwise, more conservatively, if that causes counsel some difficulty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us what happened next, Witness. In your own words, what happened as you were taken off that morning, and what did you see, and what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: When they lined us up in front of the building in a column, they started leading us down the Petar Drapsin Street, and then we crossed the Mustovic Street; and from Mustovic Street, we came to Bakamluk; and from Bakamluk, we continued down Kalemova Street. But they did not lead us down the public street, but rather, in between buildings, because this was a new development. So they led us in between buildings. And they brought us to the building of Parkovi i Nasadi, and from there they led us to the Velez stadium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you during that time, as far as you've taken us up until now, were you together with your husband and son?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that always the case that day, throughout that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: No. When they -- because before the Velez stadium, before we reached that, there are the university complex, and they made us stop there. There was an HVO soldier there, and he immediately separated men from women and children. The small children remained with their mothers, and the older ones went with their fathers, and then they were taken to the stadium, which is very close to the university. And we were all taken to the amphitheatre. We were there for perhaps an hour. And from there, that is, a soldier came and told us to get out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just so the record is clear - Mr. President, you may -- you and Your Honours may recognise this - when you say they kept you at the amphitheatre, which group were you now talking about? Is this after the men had been separated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes. Only women and children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you say, then, this HVO - excuse me - this HVO told you -- asked you to leave or told you to get out. What happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: When we left the amphitheatre, we came out onto the street, and a great number of buses was parked there, and we were ordered to board them, so that the men stayed back in the stadium and we went onward to the Rondo. And from the Rondo, we turned towards Balinovac, and from Balinovac to Masline, which is a Catholic cemetery. And then we went through a part of the city which I did not know that well any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, allow me to ask you a question before you get too far ahead. When you were around the area of the cemetery, did you observe anyone taking photographs or a recording, filming what was happening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes. In a wooded area, as I was sitting next to the window, I noticed a white UNPROFOR vehicle, and from that, next to the vehicle, was a soldier. He wasn't that far away. He was standing and recording, I guess, the people as they were being taken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then as you proceeded through this part of the city that you said you were not familiar with, or the area -- and you don't need to tell us all the details there, I don't think. Just take us on. Did you take us on through that? Did you come to an area some distance from the Heliodrom? And then tell us what happened then.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Because I did not know at all where we were going, I heard people murmuring in the bus, people who were there with me, "If you don't stop us at Miljkovici, then we are going to Ljubuski. If they stop us at Miljkovici, then we will certainly be taken to the Heliodrom." And indeed, when we arrived in Miljkovici buses were stopped there. We were let out of the buses. We walked awhile, and then we were brought to a road which was just new, recently made, and I was told that it was called the Varda road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you, the group of you, then told at some point then to walk, to finish, in fact to walk to the Heliodrom? And did you do so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Right. From Miljkovici, we went on foot to the Heliodrom, right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct that you then were held at the Heliodrom until approximately the 15th or 16th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a few questions about the time that you were held there. Can you tell the Judges, please, approximately how many people, prisoners, people that were being held did you see at the Heliodrom at that time? And I'm not asking for a precise number, but can you give the Judges whether it was a small group of people or a large group of people or your estimate, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Very large, because you know, later on they brought the men from the stadium, and it was full. I think that we were over 20.000 Muslims who were detained there. We were a very large number, men, women, and children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the names of any of the soldiers or others who guarded you during the time that you were held at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: At the Heliodrom, I saw Mr. Ante Buhovac, and I know that there was another gentleman named Stanko, a younger man, a soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall while you were held there seeing any other persons, HVO officers or officials, who you recognised or came to know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Of the HVO? Later on Mr. Misic came, on the 15th and 16th, I believe. So Mr. Misic came to the room once, and he identified himself as Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Major Misic, that he had come to visit us and see how we were doing. At that time, all the women -- because my room was full of women where I was, so all the women asked him why they were not going home, what they were doing there, what they were supposed to do there. And Mr. Misic told them -- actually, told us - because we were all there - that the war was raging in Mostar and that they had moved us from Mostar in order to protect us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the women follow that answer up with any further questions or comments to Mr. Misic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: They did. A lady asked him why we, why the Muslims, if they were trying to protect people, why did they not bring Croat women along too, because that would have made sense. However, he again repeated that there was a war going on in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Before moving on with the time that you were released then, let me just ask again if you remember -- do you remember seeing any other HVO officers at the Heliodrom during this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: I don't understand. What do you mean, "officers"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's go to when you were released. You've said you were released sometime around the 15th or 16th of May, 1993. Around that day, did a group of people come to the prison? And tell the Chamber how it was, what happened during the time that you were released.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: After Mr. Misic arrived and after our conversation with him, perhaps an hour later two soldiers came - his bodyguards probably, because they had come with him the first time around - and they told us that who had no one who was a member of the ABiH, that those can go home, so that we had to cross over into another building to give some kind of statements. This was the first time. When I entered that building, it was a large room like this, and the tables were arranged in a semi-circle, and a lot of people were sitting there. In the corner, I recognised Mr. [redacted]. He was just sitting there, saying nothing. And Mr. Misic was also there. And I

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
