utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't know if those would tend to identify, but again, out of an abundance of caution, if they could be redacted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the Judges, at this point in the trial, have heard the name [redacted] associated with a number of individuals, at least -- I won't comment further. But do you know -- do you have a first name, or can you provide the Chamber with a bit more information on the [redacted] who you said you saw in this room on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: No. I mean, I really can't remember the name, [redacted] [redacted]. We lived in the same building. He worked for the state security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Otherwise, he was a soldier in the Croatian army, because he had those Croatian insignia at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, obviously we're going to require some redactions on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I know it's getting late in the day and this is stressful for you, and again I apologise, but please don't use any names or say where you live or who your neighbours are, because again, this would tend to identify who you are. So we're going to ask the record to be corrected so that will not be broadcast. But if you could be mindful of that, please. Thank you. All right. One final question about this [redacted] and then we'll go forward. You said a moment ago that he was in the Croatian army. Now, are you using that term specifically to mean the army of the Republic of Croatia or just a member of some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, let me help my learned friend. [redacted] So for the Prosecutor, the previous question, [redacted] if you look at the last two sentences. Because the names sound very similar, [redacted], and the witness is speaking about [redacted] all the time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. I said [redacted]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Should we go to private session for a moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It may be easier, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to the private session. Mr. Scott, you may ask this question again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were released from the Heliodrom around this time, were you able to go back to your apartment? And again, I'm going to caution you: Please don't identify, by address or location, your apartment. But were you able to go back to your apartment after being released?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: From the Heliodrom, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell the Chamber, please: What did you find there? What was the condition of your apartment, your flat, when you returned to it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Well, you know, I opened the door, and straight away I saw that all my electric appliances were gone. There was only furniture, I mean heavy pieces of furniture: wardrobes, a couch, a sofa, things like that. But the electrical appliances, they were not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Just a bit of clarification. When you say "electrical appliances," what kinds of things are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: The TV set, video, music appliances, washing machine, cooking stove, refrigerator; all the household appliances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell the Chamber, please: When you returned, did you have occasion to talk to your neighbours, and did you find out whether the same thing had happened in their flats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Well, you know, as we were still very much afraid, we used to meet, to go to one another, and I could see that from other flats more or less the same things were missing. Only two flats had been devastated because shots were fired at the walls and lots of furniture was destroyed. Other flats had not been damaged as such, but all of those electric appliances were missing from them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the time that you were arrested on the 9th of May, and then when you returned to your apartment sometime around the 15th or 16th of May, around that time, were you able to determine or observe whether any of the mosques in Mostar, the condition of those mosques, had changed between the 9th of May and the 15th or 16th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: When I returned from the Heliodrom, across the area [redacted] [redacted] and the mosque in Balinovac too. And even later on, and when I went out, I could see that the mosque across the street from the church had also been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And Witness, is it your testimony to the Chamber, then, that so far as you know and to the best that you can recall, all three of those mosques had still been intact as of the 9th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Witness, very briefly here, I'm not going to cover these next items in any detail at all, and if counsel will allow, I will just simply ask you this: Some days thereafter, a few days after you were released, is it correct that your husband was also then released for a time and also your son, and the three of you were then living for a time in the apartment again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: That's right. My husband was released seven days after me. And my son came with me because he was underage. Not only my husband; all men who had been imprisoned at the Heliodrom were released, because at that time, the Heliodrom was visited by Mr. Morillion and the Red Cross. And it was when he -- at his intervention, they were all released, so that as of the 21st, we were all together again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I can inquire, please. I know we took the last break a bit early. I'm about to change topics. I wondered what the Chamber's plans were in terms of scheduling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we could have a break right now, and we will resume at twenty to 6:00. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That would be fine, Your Honour. And I can tell the Chamber that after the break then, I would expect to complete the direct examination in fairly short order. I would say another 15, 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could the usher pull down the blinds and take the witness out first. Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. We didn't quite understand. Shall we have a break until twenty to 8:00 -- excuse me, twenty to 6:00? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will resume at twenty to 6:00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'd like to comment at the beginning that I'm sorry to cause some exasperation for your staff. Obviously sometimes we're caught between trying as much of the trial to be public as possible and the administration of the security measures. And I apologise for any inconvenience that was caused to the Registry about that. We tried not to go into private session any more than is necessary. So I'm sorry for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I want to direct your attention now to the 13th of June, 1993. Can you tell us what happened to you and your family that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: That day, on the 13th of June, at 4.00 in the afternoon, I had come out on the balcony to put out the laundry, and then I realised that there was no cars down there. However, when I got the third batch of my laundry which I wanted to hang up, I looked down to the parking lot again, and it was full of cars. And at some point, I spotted Dolma - because after the first meeting, somehow his face had remained imprinted on my memory - and I saw him taking a rifle out of the car, and I panicked immediately because I did not think that anything good was in store for us. And when Dolma entered the building next to mine, a gentleman with two children whom he was holding by the hands came out of that building, and he was trying to tell me something, but I couldn't make out what he was telling me. And at some moment, I looked at him more carefully, and I realised that he was telling me they are driving us away. So I left my laundry on the balcony and entered the room, and from there into the living-room. And I wanted to rouse my husband, but they were already knocking on the door. And then I saw HVO soldiers there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. When this -- I'm going to ask you to continue on with your story. I'm going to caution you again - and I apologise - but not to use any names at this point. I may come back to you in a few minutes, and we go into private session, ask you for some names, but if you could continue, please, in your story without telling us the names of any family members or neighbours, I would ask that you do that, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: An HVO soldier entered my apartment and asked for our identity cards, so I gave them to him. And he read them, and then he said, "Sorry. I am sorry, but I have to put you out. And if I don't do that, then they will kill me." And my husband then said to him not to worry, that we would leave, and so we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went out of your apartment, did you again see a group of Bosniak people who had been gathered outside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes. They were all my neighbours from neighbouring buildings, or rather, from the first part of the building, which they had presumably already cleansed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any other HVO members or soldiers at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: I did. I once again recognised Mr. Takac, Mr. Stela. I've already mentioned Mr. Dolma, and there were more of them. But fearful as I was, I stopped paying attention and trying to see who those people were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I'm going to ask you a question now similar to the one I asked you earlier this afternoon. Based on your observation of what was happening at that time, can you make any -- can you provide the Chamber any assistance with whether one of these HVO soldiers appeared to be in charge of what was happening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stela.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And perhaps you can tell the Chamber a bit more about that. What did you see and hear or observe that causes you to come to that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: The gentleman was standing in the passage between the buildings, and we had to communicate with him, to give him our IDs, which were then thrown in a place and then burnt. And then I saw when a gentleman came out, he pointed something to him, and Mr. Stela got angry and started beating him. I mean, not -- that is, pushing him, shaking him, not hitting him. I don't know really how to put it, but he was really not behaving nicely, because that gentleman was an elderly man and a sick Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. man. But all the soldiers, all the HVO soldiers, spoke to him, so that one could easily see that this gentleman was leading that operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this time I would ask to go into private session for a few minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness WW, we're now back in open session, and so I'm not going to ask you to say anything more about your location at this moment. You've now moved some distance away from where you were previously located. Once you got to the church, however, tell us again what happened then next.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: I've told you: They lined us up, and when they saw that that area was clear -- and before that, as we were passing by a high-rise, a lady happened to look through the window, and one of the soldiers let out such a burst of fire that I still do not know whether this lady is still alive. And that really upset us. And then when we reached the church, they lined us up against the church wall. When they saw that the area was clear, they forced us to run for what we are worth to the area of Semovac, that is, the area held by the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once you were in the area controlled by the ABiH -- by the ABiH - excuse me - were you then kept and provided for for a time in a school in that part of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: I forgot to say when they made us run. The HVO soldier who had escorted us fired after us, and at the same time the fire started from the hill of Hum, so the BH army, not knowing what was going on, opened fire too, so that we were caught in all this fire and crossfire. And when we got out from the area, we were still in view of the BH army. Then they stopped firing because they realised that we were civilians. And at Semovac, there are some new white buildings, and that is where they took us in in the beginning. After that, they took us to Mahala, to the local school there where there was some centre or some infirmary or something. I don't know what to call it. And they kept us there for a while until they took our names down and as they were trying to find some normal - I mean "normal," in quotation marks - accommodation. And people in Mahala shortly opened all their homes and all the space available to them and offered it to the evicted people, so that very few people remained behind in the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell the Chamber: Was there a problem with keeping people at the school because more and more people would arrive day by day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes. Not only during the day, because this cleansing, the second one, started at 4.00 on the 13th of June. So from 4.00 onward until late into the night, people were arriving in large, large numbers. That is, they must have been cleansing borough after borough, that is, one settlement after another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to take you into private session in a moment for a few final details, but before I do that, as you were gathered outside and before you went off to the church and the confrontation line, can you tell the Judges, please, who was it that ordered that you be taken to cross the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: To go and stand in front of the building, that was Mr. Stela who ordered this. And who ordered them? Well, I don't know. Somebody must have ordered them. To start from the building to the church, I think it was Mr. Stela. Now, I don't think, I'm [Realtime transcript read in error "not"] quite sure, because he was number one. Everybody listened to what he had to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct, Witness, then, that you then stayed in this area of Mostar during the duration of the war between the Croats and Bosniaks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to have the witness shown a -- one of the street diagrams. However, I'm told by your staff that it may be difficult to do that without it being broadcast, so it may be that we have to go into closed session for this particular part. I'm happy to do it either -- any way that will protect the witness, if there's some way of doing it without going into completely closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, but there's a question which I'm not quite clear. On the line 58, line 2, the witness said, "Now, I don't think, I'm not sure," but I heard just the opposite.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, thank you very much. I -- I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think the witness said, "I'm quite sure." You may ask her this question again before we go to the closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. I heard the same thing, and that's why it didn't even occur to me, frankly, to look down at the transcript. And I appreciate Your Honour's assistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness WW, there may be just a recording matter here. You said a moment ago -- I asked you the question about who had ordered these things to happen. Initially you said you thought -- but what did -- what is your answer? Maybe -- perhaps you can just say in your own words again. Do you know who it was who ordered that you be taken, the group of you be taken to the church and to cross the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Stela. Mr. Stela ordered us to move on, and the soldiers who were escorting us, they ordered us to cross the line. Now -- and their names, I don't know, believe me, but I'm quite sure Mr. Stela was the one who ordered in front of the building to take us towards the church so that we would then cross to the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And then if I could have the assistance, please, to put Exhibit P11.18, 11.18 in front of the witness but in such a way that it would not be displayed outside the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I only thought it was appropriate. That ends my questions, but I thought it was appropriate that I thank the witness for her testimony publicly. Witness WW, thank you very much for coming to The Hague. I'm sorry if anything that I've asked you has caused you any suffering, but we appreciate your testimony. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any cross-examination? Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. Seric:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, I'm Branko Seric, and I am the Defence counsel for Mr. Vinko Martinovic. In your evidence, you said that you had heard the last name Martinovic in connection to the HOS units in Mostar. Do you know that in this HOS unit, there were 80 per cent of Muslims and 20 per cent of Croats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness come closer to the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the HOS played a positive role in the struggle against the JNA and for the liberation of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Well, probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it because of this, or was that the reason that this name, Vinko Martinovic, became not only well known but perhaps even popular in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that on 9 May 1993 you were in your apartment and that you heard the shelling. Can you tell us, at least approximately - I know that more than eight years have gone by - what time it was when you heard it and what did it look like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: What time it was? It was around 5.00 in the morning, five minutes plus or minus, and the shelling was terrible. And the left bank was targeted. Not the part of town where I lived, but the shelling was targeting exclusively the left bank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that? Did you see that? How do you know about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Because no shell fell into my neighbourhood, so that made me believe -- so that was clear to me that they were not shelling the part of town where more or less -- that was Croatia, and on the left bank there was the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that around 6.00 in the morning seven soldiers knocked on your door and that you recognised some among them. Regardless what you saw on television or in the media or what you know today, can you go back to that day now in your mind and describe to us the physical appearance of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the person whom you referred to as Vinko Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: This person was kind of bald -- actually, not balding, but had his hair cropped. He had an earring, and he had black gloves with the fingers cut off, and he was carrying a weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old could he have been at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Really, I don't know. I assume 35 to 40. I don't know. I think approximately that age.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that today he would be between 45 and 50?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: If you add ten years, that would be about that figure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe, if you remember this detail, in which ear he had his earring?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: No. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And will you please wait, ma'am, because if you cut in before I finish my question, your voice will be picked up by my microphone and then all the protective measures will have been for naught. Can you describe, can you recall what Ernest Takac looked like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: He had long hair and a beard. The hair was not washed, so he was dirty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How tall was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just sort of estimate it according to me? Taller or shorter than I am?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: He was taller than I am, but I don't know in relation to you. I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long was his beard, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: I don't know. Not like yours. It wasn't like yours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that it was longer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes, it was a bit longer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you learn that it was this person who was named Takac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: When Mr. Stela called him. Because when Mr. Takac attacked the journalist, he told him, "Takac, don't touch him."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What would you tell me if I were to tell you that Vinko Martinovic never wore an earring and that he doesn't have any pierced ears?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Nothing, sir, and you don't have to have a pierced ear to be wearing an earring. You can have a clip on your ear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You will agree with me that a soldier who is moving about all day, that he would be wearing such type of an earring that could fall off his ear at any point. You also mentioned the name Benito Sesar. How did this person look?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Benito was dark, middle-aged. And, you know, they were all wearing uniforms, so I wouldn't be able to give you a detailed description. We were all in fear, and his name was also mentioned, Benito's. And the people in the neighbourhood sort of knew each other. They knew how people looked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know at that time, or perhaps today, is it known to you today, to which unit did these soldiers, and including Mr. Martinovic, belong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: To be honest with you, I did not know that at the time when I was kicked out of the house, but at the Heliodrom, obviously we started talking about things, so that the people who knew him, who had known him from before, said that he belonged to the ATG, the anti-terrorist group. I think that that's what it was called. But I believe that that's what people said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ma'am, do you remember that on the 26th September, 1998, you gave a statement to the investigators of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this statement, you said that later on at the Heliodrom, learned, as you said now, that they had belonged to the 4th Battalion, in a conversation with the other women, because that same group had come to their houses [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, just so that you do not misunderstand my motions with the hand, I'm not threatening you in any way. I'm just signalling you to wait for me to finish. Ma'am, did you see some kind of characteristic patches, insignia on their shoulders, chests, or sleeves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes. The HVO soldiers, on their left sleeve, they had a patch. Now, I know that it was the HVO on it, there was a checkerboard there and something crossed. I don't know if theirs were rifles or swords. And then there was laurel branches underneath. I mean, this is what I recall. But as I said, I was in terrible fear at the time. But I think -- in fact, I don't think I saw that. I remember the checkerboard. It was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your examination-in-chief by my learned friend Mr. Scott, you -- when you talked about their first appearance at your apartment, the first contact with your husband with -- with the taking off of the plaque and being called balijas, and all that time you mentioned Takac in relation to all these actions. Now, I'm a bit surprised. On the basis of what did you infer, because you said that in your evidence, that Martinovic was the chief one or in charge of all this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Your -- sir, we -- my building had four floors. Mr. Stela was at the entrance door, and Mr. Takac was standing in front of my door while the other soldiers went upstairs. But all the orders, believe me, were issued by Mr. Stela, because all the soldiers who were coming downstairs after we had come out, they were all coming to him and they were telling him that everything was all right, that there were no Muslims left, that all apartments have been cleared of Muslims. So it was -- it was clear from all that that Mr. Stela was commanding or leading that action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you able to hear all these orders, all these alleged orders by Mr. Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: I heard when they entered. They all entered the building together, and I was the first one there. My apartment was the first. And then the gentleman told them to go upstairs. He -- Mr. Takac stayed at my apartment, and the rest of them went upstairs. But when -- as they all came back downstairs, they all addressed him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you trying to say now that Martinovic did not enter your apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I did not understand your answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: No, Mr. Stela did not enter my apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now it is clear. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: On the 9th of May, he did not enter my apartment. He stayed in front of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let me take you back to my original question. You said that you had heard his orders. How were you in a position to hear them if you spent part of the time in your apartment and only then you came out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: No, sir. I was at the door to my apartment when I came out, because as soon as he kicked out my husband -- as soon as he called him by his name -- said his name, Takac kicked him out. And I walked out behind him. You see, I was the first one. Everybody else lives above me. And the other soldiers were there, and he said, "Go up and look if there are others there." And Mr. Takac stayed back to see that we were leaving the apartment. So he was standing by my door, and Mr. Stela was standing by the entrance to the building while the other soldiers were cleansing the rest of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know that it is terrible for you to go through this, to relive this experience again.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: It's awful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it is very hard for me to conduct this cross-examination, because I am not disputing your experience at all. I am just trying to clear up everybody's role in this. You mention now the entrance to the building. Now, in relationship to this entrance, where did you observe Mr. Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: At the -- at the door, the entrance door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean at the very entrance door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes, at the entrance door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this mean that your observation of this man Martinovic and his description is the -- is your observation that he was standing at the door as you walked past him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes. And the encounter with Mr. [redacted], because they were both very close.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, do you know or did you see -- I would like to know your personal experience. This person of whom you say that it was Mr. Martinovic and the description that you gave --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting, Your Honour. I thought perhaps Mr. Seric was going to correct this himself and that is the reason I hesitated. I was looking across the room. But the name -- the one name was mentioned again, and I'm sorry, we'll have to have that redacted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, my learned friend. I had just received warning myself. So you overtook me. But let me move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see that this Martinovic enter any of the apartments in that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: You mean in my building? No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that there is another person with the same name, Vinko Martinovic, in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, indeed there was another Vinko Martinovic who was a soldier.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes, but I do know this Vinko Martinovic here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A little while ago, you mentioned a person, a neighbour. Don't mention his name, and I won't. And then you said in your examination-in-chief that the appearance of this neighbour provoked Mr. Martinovic to take some action, and then there was that incident with this Mercedes car. You mentioned that. Do you know what was talked about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: The keys.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were the keys?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: He did not have the keys on him. And when Mr. Stela asked for the keys, he said he didn't have them on him. But the Mercedes could also be switched on with a wire or something. I don't know exactly. I mean, I know nothing about these things, so I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see who got into that car and put together those wires?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: A soldier. I don't know which one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did this soldier also drive that car away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you saw that same vehicle. Now I forget the exact date, but it doesn't matter. You said that you saw that vehicle again as you were coming back from work, that you saw it on fire. Could you please explain what it was all about. Did you mean to say that it had been set on fire, that you saw flames?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: As I came up, coming back from work, the car was on fire. How and what, I don't really know, but the car was on fire. I don't know what it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe the exact position of that vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Across the street from a coffee-shop on the old playground, old playground -- or as a matter of fact, new buildings had been built there, and there were coffee-shops on both sides. So it was on the opposite side, on the pavement, on the sidewalk. That car was on the opposite pavement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what coffee-shop are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Oh, I don't know. I don't know what its name is because it's on the opposite -- on the opposite side from the one that I used. Because I was walking along the pavement, and I think that Mr. Stela had taken over the coffee-shop that belonged earlier to somebody, I believe, called Mr. Kovacevic, and I saw him a couple of times in that coffee-shop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know all this about this coffee-shop? This coffee-shop was under communist regime, the socially owned property, and it belonged to Mr. Vinko Martinovic's father.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Which coffee-shop are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The one that you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: But I'm talking about Mr. Kovacevic's coffee-shop. I suppose Mr. Martinovic knows that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is this coffee-shop?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Well, it is there on Strelcevina. It's the old Velez pitch.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please help me to show the witness this map once again, 11.18. Oh, I see, yes. Could we go into closed session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, let us try to clear up certain matters relating to the incident of the 13th of June, 1993. You mentioned names of people, and what I'd like to know is: How could it be that on both occasions it was the same people, on the 9th of May and the 13th of June? How is it that it was those same men who came to your door? How could that happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Believe me, that baffles me too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today you said, and you answered me too -- and in your statement that you gave on the 26th of September, 1998, you also said about this incident of the 13th of June, that those soldiers were members of the 4th Battalion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: I think so. I think it is, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the commander of the 4th Battalion was Mladen Misic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Well, I know he was, because at the time when I worked, Mr. Misic had his battalion at Rondo, and he was the commander of the 4th Battalion, because I passed that way every day, and I saw him there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that Mladen Misic's soldiers were under what command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you be more precise? You said that Martinovic was standing in a passage between buildings and that he began to behave wrongly, and then you proceeded to describe how roughly he treated that gentleman. I won't mention his name. So I'll say he was a manager - I won't mention of what - so that we don't have to go into private session. But can you tell me, how far were you from them at that moment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Mr. Stela - since my locality is in residential blocks, and one residential block has four buildings, and then you have a passage or a street, and then another block of four buildings, and I lived in that second block - and Mr. Stela came and stood right between those two blocks, in that passage between those two buildings. And my front door is somewhere there. So when I crossed the lawn, I fetched up in the street, so that practically it was not far. It was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us how many metres? Ten, twelve, two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there people? Were there any obstacles, anything that obstructed your view?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: No. We were all in this one line in front of those buildings, and the gentleman stood right between those buildings, so that we could see -- so that we could all see very well what he was doing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, now, you say "all." And so could you see well what he was doing? Could you then tell us, if you remember, what exactly was going on? What did this manager point at? What kind of personal document? What was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: I don't really know. Believe me, I don't really know. I merely saw Mr. Stela shove him, push him, then hit him. I mean, he really treated him very roughly. How to put it? He beat him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that the reason for Mr. Vinko Martinovic's reaction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: I don't know. I saw that he was trying to show him something that he held in his hand, and I just assumed that that was the reason, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know what happened to this gentleman later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Well, he wasn't beaten that badly so that that would disable him. He could move, and he came to me, because his wife was standing next to me, and we were taken towards the church all together, all together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said he wasn't beaten all that badly, in the first description. As a matter of fact, you said that he pushed him, he shoved him, that there were no direct blows, but that he was pushing him, shoving him, and kicking him, and you said that you were near enough that nothing obstructed your view. Tell me, please: I know that it was many years ago, but it is very important for us for you to tell us. Did this man sustain any injuries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Well, not too bad, not any that would prevent him from moving. He could walk, even though he had been beaten. He was beaten. I cannot say that he battered him so that he fell to the ground, but he beat him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any bruises on him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Oh, listen. I was on one side, and he went to the other side, and at that moment, sir, I could not see anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But was there any blood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: No, there was no blood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said -- we heard from you about the incident on the 9th of May and the 13th of June, and you mentioned those four names that you mentioned, that is, Martinovic, Takac, Sesar, and the nickname Dolma. Since you know those four names, do you know the name of at least one other soldier whom you knew or whom you recognised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any soldiers with white belts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: On the 13th of June or on the 9th of May?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Either.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: I didn't see them. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anyone in a black uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who that was or how many of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: On the 9th of May, Mr. Takac was in a black uniform, and on the 13th of June, I really don't know if there were any. I just don't know, on the 13th of June. On the 9th of May, four of them were in these uniforms and others were in many-coloured uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice if those other soldiers, whether they came from your area, from your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell them? Could you really somehow identify them by their dialect or something? Because we all speak our dialects. I come from Split, and I have my dialect. You speak your Mostar dialect. Could you see if any of them were not from Mostar? If you heard them speak, could you recognise the dialects?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. We are dealing with two different dates, but somehow the events are similar. So I don't want to confuse you and jump from the 9th of May to the 13th of June, so let me talk about the 9th of May. Tell me, could you say if it was one unit or several different units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: I don't know. I just don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would the same answer apply to the 13th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes, because, you know, I only saw Stela. I didn't see other people, because they had dispersed all over the building, so I cannot say whether those were those same units. I really don't know. But they were soldiers. They were army men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those four surnames that you gave us, did you learn all these four names later on, after you arrived at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Well, yes. You know, I was completely addled by this whole situation, but at the Heliodrom, we had lots of time. And people who were at the Heliodrom already, they already knew everybody, and they talked, and they invariably mentioned Mr. Stela, and Mr. Takac, and Dolma, and so on. They mentioned other people too, but I just can't remember it, because after all, it was a long time. But Mr. Stela's name I really do remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us about what you heard at the Heliodrom? Did you hear it from persons who had shared your lot, that is, who is been evicted from your building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Well, those who were evicted from all the flats, because the Heliodrom were not only people from my building, there were people from Panjevina, from Balinovac, and from other areas. They were not only -- because they were not taking people out of my neighbourhood only. They were taking people from all the neighbourhoods, from all the localities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the examination-in-chief, you said that -- and you were speaking about the 13th of June, and you said that Stela led the operation. Do you remember -- do you remember how many soldiers were there altogether to cover all those buildings and all this whole event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Well, as I told you, when I looked out and saw cars parked, there were very many, very many cars parked, because they were not closing only my building. They had started from the first residential block and then moved on, so that I cannot really tell you how many soldiers there were, but them I saw. Them I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, from your story, should one conclude that Vinko Martinovic commanded all those men who were there at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, the separation in Mostar that was established, that was already there on the 13th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Yes, Bulevar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which part of the -- which sector of that line was held by the unit commanded by Vinko Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Oh, no. No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know -- are you aware that that part -- that this part of the town in which you lived was not under the jurisdiction, if I may put it that way, of the -- Vinko Martinovic's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that on that day, the 13th of June, a part of the unit, one-third of the unit, was manning a sector of this line on the Bulevar facing the BH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the number of -- how strong was Vinko Martinovic's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for your safety, madam, don't speak before I switch off. What I'm trying to say -- that is what I'm trying to ask you. You yourself said that it was a large number of soldiers on that occasion and that they were all commanded by Vinko Martinovic. Now, if it is a fact that at that time there was a separation line, that a part of that line was manned by a third or maybe even more men from Vinko Martinovic's unit, then I'm telling you that it was physically impossible for such a large part of the unit to come to your neighbourhood under the command of Vinko Martinovic. And what will you tell me to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Sir, I don't know how many soldiers there were, 10, 15. I do not know how many there were. I do not know. What I do know is that Mr. Stela led that operation both on the first occasion and on the second occasion, and that is all that I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement of the 26th of September, 1998, you say at some point that -- now, let me give you the whole sentence. "When they stopped beating them ..." and I'm referring to neighbours. We shall not mention their names --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I didn't say anything the first time because I wasn't sure. I was going to give some latitude, but I think it's only fair to this witness that the statement be put in front of her and she be able to see the statement if she's going to be questioned about it, please. If counsel doesn't, I have an extra B/C/S version that I can tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now, that's not the first time that we've come across this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the first time I'm doing this, and I do have the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but you are sharing the same desk, bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, both of the same feather. Yes, we say that too. My apologies. I don't know if I have enough copies, Your Honours. Would you like to have copies in English?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So let me finish this part, the statement, and then we'll continue tomorrow. So page 7, sixth line from the bottom. The sentence begins: "When they stopped beating them, they ordered us to turn, faces to the building." Now, my question is: How long did it last? How long did you stand facing the building, or rather, the first part of my question is how far were you from the building, from the building wall, and how long did you stay lined up in this manner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: From the wall, from the building, because this is a very small area, it's a very narrow street, so we could have been about half a metre away from the building because we were very many in this line. And we stood there for about five minutes, until we were all lined up, and then they told us to turn towards the church.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did this -- all this last when you came out of the building and they lined you up? You said five minutes, but how long did this whole procedure last?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: Well, if they arrived at around 4.00 in the afternoon, around 1600, it could have lasted until about half past 4.00. I'm not sure. But there were very many people. They had evicted very many people. So I don't know exactly how long it took, but -- how long it took, but it could Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. have been about half an hour, perhaps 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And all that time, you could watch all that was going on, even at the time whilst you had to face the wall and all that allowed you to conclude that Vinko Martinovic commanded all that action?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS WW
utterances.text: No, sir. We all watched Mr. Stela do that. And when that was all over, it was then that we were ordered to turn and face the wall, so that by the time we are up and aligned and by the time we were all turned, not to the other side but then we had to turn towards the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. I do not know. Shall we call it a day and resume tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, I'm afraid that we have to keep you for another day here. We will continue tomorrow afternoon. During your stay here, please do not talk to anybody about your testimony, and do not let anybody talk to you, as I remind other witnesses. Usher, will you please take the witness out of the courtroom first?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm sorry to take more of your time because your working day is over, but there is something that troubles me. Excuse me. My first question is: Have you received our motion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Which motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We filed a motion today. We have received the receipt, so we thought that you had already received it. That is, we were making a submission because tomorrow a witness was announced, Mr. Prelec. I don't think he's protected. Our learned friends have announced him as a witness, and we wanted to ask you and explain in this submission the reasons for which we should like him to testify not tomorrow but after the holidays, because if we understood well our learned friends, he should testify to -- he should be testifying about a major area which we have not managed to study properly now because it is a very bulky material. It is the transcripts concerning the material from the office of the president of the republic. Yes, we received it a month ago. I hope my learned friend won't say anything. Yes, I confirm we received it a month ago and so on and so forth, but we simply -- all this material - and my learned friend can help me - there must be a thousand pages to it, and for the past month, we have not found time to go through it, and I'm not ready to conduct any cross-examination of Mr. Prelec, so we wanted to ask you now that the holidays are coming up - and of course it will be working holidays for us - to spend the holidays studying this material so that we could both follow the examination-in-chief and, of course, conduct the cross-examination. Now, if you have not received our submission yet, then could we please have the answer tomorrow? But then again, we'd need your answer today, your ruling today if -- or perhaps the Prosecution can conduct the direct examination, but then could we at least cross-examine this witness after the holidays?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] Frankly speaking, we haven't received that motion yet. Let us hear the response from the Prosecutor on this very issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think -- I hope the Chamber knows by now that we have tried to conduct this trial in an effective and efficient way as possible and met our disclosure obligations, I think, very faithfully, if I can say so. I do appreciate that counsel does acknowledge receiving those materials a month ago, at least a month ago. It may be closer to six weeks ago. In addition to that, I specifically provided a letter to counsel some weeks ago anticipating that we would in fact reach this witness on approximately the week of the 12th of November. Again, we didn't do that. But, Mr. President and Your Honours, this witness has been on notice and this evidence has been on hold, if you will, or been proposed for a long time. There's been a full opportunity for counsel to be prepared to meet this witness. In fact, again that was exactly -- my forecast, my prediction, I'm afraid, has come true, because the very reason that I made -- took pains to give this other notice - and I have the letter, and if necessary I'll provide it to the Chamber - is that there would be completely fair notice some weeks before this evidence was led. Now, I think there's been absolutely fair and abundant notice to allow counsel to prepare. Of course we're all busy. The Prosecution is very busy too and is trying to bring this -- its case to a close as soon as possible. Now, secondly, Mr. Prelec is being proposed as a document foundation witness, and this brings us back to what has happened with Mr. Prelec and also happened with Mr. Aguirre. These men are not proposed as expert witnesses. They are proposed and have been tendered to the Chamber simply to introduce the documents and to show how the documents were obtained, what the documents purport to be. I expect that my direct examination tomorrow will probably be not more than a -- much more than an hour. It is simply to say, "Here are the bundle of documents. Can you explain to the Chamber, please, how these documents came into the hands of the OTP, what the documents purport to be, give the Chamber some overall orientation to the documents," but it is not again, once again, the purpose of this witness to go into any lengthy analysis of the material. And as we saw before, I will object very much to questions by counsel going into -- trying to cross-examine this witness on the merits, if you will, the substance of this material. So -- which brings me to say that counsel, for these purposes, doesn't need to be prepared to go through every page, if that's what he says he has to do. But again I come back to my prior point: This material has been available for something in excess of a month, and we are prepared to go forward, Your Honour. We must conclude our case. There's been due notice, and the witness has properly understood, has properly understood the scope of his testimony, can easily be dealt with by counsel tomorrow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could I ask another question? Do you have any other witnesses besides the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: There is -- sorry. There's one more witness here this week, and depending on how things go, we would be prepared to have a witness on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. Could we have that witness tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I believe we probably could, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Because we need some time, you know, to consider the request from the Defence counsel, and as well as your objections on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, let me address the Chamber further on this, then. If we do not take this evidence before Christmas -- and frankly, I'm a bit disappointed if that happens, because I had intended to lead that evidence a long time ago, and because of scheduling, it hasn't been. So I'll have to tell the Chamber, I would be disappointed if we didn't do it before Christmas. The problem that poses in particular is, as the Chamber knows, I expect this will be one of those instances in which the Defence will then ask for 30 days to respond to these exhibits. If we don't do this until January, that will then put us well into the month of February. And again, as I've said before, with all respect, every respect to the Chamber, Mr. President, Your Honours, we're not going to be in a position to rest our case until we know that the exhibits have been properly received or that we've been able to take any steps necessary to make sure, as much as possible, that our evidence will be accepted. So if we do not accept this evidence now -- and I submit it's very important evidence. These are transcripts from the offices of the President of the Republic of Croatia, former President Tudjman, of conversations in his office that show very clearly the existence of an international armed conflict that was controlled, in large measure, from Zagreb. It's very important that the Chamber receive this evidence, and I'm concerned about postponing it until January. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that you still have the chance to come back to certain documents which were not admitted by this Chamber during the rebuttal procedures, after the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would -- the practice in the Tribunal that I'm familiar with has been that Chambers have shown to be quite conservative in their treatment of rebuttal cases, and I would frankly be a bit concerned. Obviously, I'm in the Chamber's hands. If you give me some assurances that in fact that would be the case, then I certainly will accept the Chamber's guidance on that. But I would be -- my general reaction would be one of some concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my apologies once again, but this is a very important matter, and I believe it is my duty to tell you what this is about. It is my duty to tell you that these documents are of major importance for us, and I was happy to hear my learned friend confirm that, because if they're important for our learned friends, that is, for the Prosecution, they are just as -- even more important for us. Your Honours, there was an attempt to introduce these documents during the Kordic/Cerkez case, and were not admitted then because the Chamber refused to do that, because the Chamber was not quite clear about all the circumstances, and they were not admitted into evidence by that Chamber. Now we -- first an attempt is made to introduce here the transcripts of testimonies, and we have already reasoned the motion objection to the admittance of these transcripts. In this manner, we want the witnesses to be brought in. So this is a subject which is very broad, which is very important for us, and something that we have to study. Yes, I admit that I received it six weeks ago. Yes, I admit that. But believe me, I have no time to sleep since July. I have no time to sleep. For the past several weeks, I have not had time to read anything but the pages for the next witness and the witness coming up the next day. And I'm sorry. Perhaps I -- I said I don't sleep. Perhaps I'm exaggerating, but I'm not trying to be pathetic. I really sleep very little. I really sleep very little. I don't have time for much sleep, and that is the truth. And you understand that these holidays will not be holidays. Everybody else will be enjoying Christmas, their Christmas, and we shall be working in order to somehow manage this pace which has been imposed on us. I simply have not had time to read a single sheet of these documents, and I do not know why the Prosecutor, who is my learned friend, who is my colleague, why -- he should not be indifferent to whether I shall be able to ask my questions and parry his questions or not, and I really do not know whether I shall be up to that, because I have not yet managed to read that. I'm sorry. Perhaps I exaggerated slightly when I speak about the time that we have available, but that is indeed so. Thank you very much. And please, once again, receive my apologies. But on the other hand, if the Prosecutor insists on the direct examination, then all right. Of course, let him conduct his direct examination. But please relieve us of the duty to conduct our cross-examination before the holidays. Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott. You know we are --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I know we're late, Your Honours, but very briefly -- I promise to be very brief. I don't want to leave one misimpression standing and unaddressed overnight. One thing, and then a second item. Counsel is correct. These transcripts were not accepted in the Kordic case but under very specific circumstances. Because we have been trying to get this material - and I'm happy to document this at length - over a long period of time. The material did not become available to the Prosecution until very late in the case; indeed, after we had rested our case in chief, which brings me back to my prior concern. And in that situation - I'm happy for the Chamber to review the record in that case - the Chamber did not receive it because it considered it out of time. There was no substantive ruling. It was not considered unreliable; it was not rejected. It was simply a scheduling matter. And I'm happy for the Chamber to review that. So I don't want there to be any wrong impression created.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down, Mr. Scott, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apology to translation. Secondly, Your Honour, as I've said before, what I'm going to ask Mr. Prelec is: How did the OTP obtain this material? Now, counsel can cross-examine him on that without reviewing 4.000 pages of transcripts. And finally - and I said I'd be short - again, Your Honours, I will not be put in the position of the bad guy here. Counsel was given this disclosure a long time ago, and I took specific pains to give notice at least six weeks ago. So I think I have been reasonably sympathetic to the needs of counsel to prepare. I think that's more than enough time to prepare. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it is really late today, and since we haven't received the submissions from Defence counsel, and we are in no position to make a decision right now, we'll come back to this tomorrow. We will adjourn until 2.30 tomorrow afternoon in Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 6th day of December 2001, at 2.30 p.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
